candidate.answerReason: The angle at B is 50°. Since DB=BE, triangle DBE has two equal base angles, each measuring 65°.

methods.label: Use the isosceles triangle
methods.explanation:
The equality \(DB=BE\) makes \(\triangle DBE\) isosceles, so finding its vertex angle at \(B\) will determine both base angles. First use the angle sum in \(\triangle ABC\):
\[
\angle ABC=180^\circ-55^\circ-75^\circ=50^\circ.
\]
Because \(D\) lies on \(AB\) and \(E\) lies on \(BC\), the angle \(\angle DBE\) is this same \(50^\circ\) angle. The equal sides \(DB\) and \(BE\) have opposite equal angles \(\angle BED\) and \(\angle BDE\). Thus
\[
\angle BED=\frac{180^\circ-50^\circ}{2}=65^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
